cities.base: Vesterbro, on the Central Station and Tivoli side, so the long train days start on foot; Indre By, Rosenborg and Nyhavn are a walk or a short ride away.
cities.name: Copenhagen

cities.base: Vasastan, for quieter streets and Lilla Ego on the corner; Hötorgshallen, Gamla stan and the Djurgården museums are a metro ride or a long walk.
cities.name: Stockholm

cities.base: Grünerløkka, then a tram in to the cathedral, Bjørvika for the Munch and Vaaghals, and the island ferries at Aker Brygge.
cities.name: Oslo

places.name: Pluto
places.note: Bib Gourmand 2026. Take the 10-course sharing menu at 595 kroner a head, ordered for the whole table; a la carte mains run 185 to 315, the lobster hot dog 245. Dinner from 17:30 every day, to 02:00 on Friday and Saturday.

places.name: Anarki
places.note: Bib Gourmand 2026 bistro in Frederiksberg. Sunday is a four-course set at 375 kroner, with paired wine for another 375; the weekday menu is a PDF and its price was not found. Shut Mondays, and Sunday closes at 21:00.

places.name: Domhusets Smørrebrød
places.note: A weekday smørrebrød counter, Google 4.8 from 481 reviews. Pieces run about 20 to 60 kroner and two make lunch; take them to a bench. Monday to Friday 07:15 to 15:00, shut weekends, and carry some cash as well as a card.

places.name: Hallernes Smørrebrød, Tivoli Food Hall
places.note: The Tivoli Food Hall branch of the smørrebrød counter, prawn and egg from 80 kroner a piece. Reviewers find it a little dear for what it is, but it runs 11:00 to 22:00, to 23:00 Friday and Saturday, after the old counters have shut.

places.name: Sporvejen
places.note: Burgers in a former tram building on Gråbrødretorv. A cheeseburger is 78 kroner in the day and 117 in the evening, so eat here at lunch. One guide gives the opening as 11:00 or 12:00 depending on the day, so check first.

places.name: Tivoli Gardens
places.note: Opened 15 August 1843; ride Rutschebanen, the wooden roller coaster from 1914, after dark. The Halloween season runs 2 October to 1 November 2026, then it reopens for Christmas. Hours and entry vary by season, so check the price on tivoli.dk.

places.name: Selma (Mikkeller taps)
places.note: Twelve Mikkeller taps on the bar side of Selma, a Bib Gourmand smørrebrød room. Lunch Wednesday to Monday 11:30 to 16:00, dinner Wednesday to Saturday to 23:00, shut Tuesdays. Prices are not published online, so check the price.

places.name: Rosenborg Castle
places.note: Christian IV's castle of 1606 to 1624, with the Crown Jewels and Regalia in the treasury. Book online, since numbers are capped and it sells out. Daily 10:00 to 17:00 until 1 November, then Tuesday to Sunday to 16:00. The price was not found, so check the price.

places.name: National Museum of Denmark
places.note: Founded 1807: the Trundholm Sun Chariot, the Egtved Girl's oak coffin, the Gundestrup cauldron and the Viking rooms. 130 kroner, free under 18. Daily 10:00 to 17:00 April to October; November to March it shuts on Mondays. Go first thing.

places.name: Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek
places.note: Carl Jacobsen's museum of 1897: Greek and Roman sculpture, the French Post-Impressionists and the Danish Golden Age. Shut Mondays; daily hours and the adult price were not found, so check the price. Free the last Wednesday of every month.

places.name: Church of Our Saviour spire
places.note: Lambert van Haven's church of 1682 to 1695, and Thurah's 1752 spire: 90m and 400 steps, the last 150 outside. Tower 70 kroner, daily 09:00 to 20:00. It shuts all January and in rain, snow or high wind, so climb on a clear morning.

places.name: Kastellet
places.note: A star fortress begun in 1626 and rebuilt after the Swedish siege of 1658 to 1660, with the 1703 Citadel Church, the prison where Struensee awaited execution and an 1847 windmill. Still a military area; hours and entry were not confirmed, so check the price.

places.name: Nyhavn
places.note: The canal dug 1670 to 1675 under Christian V by soldiers and Swedish prisoners; Hans Christian Andersen lived at number 67 and later at 18. An open street with no ticket. Walk it in the morning, before the terraces fill.

places.name: Amalienborg
places.note: The rococo palace quarter of 1750 to 1760. Be on the square at noon for the guard change; the guards march from Rosenborg at 11:30. Christian VIII's Palace holds the royal museum, whose hours and price were not found, so check the price.

places.name: Rundetaarn
places.note: Christian IV's observatory tower of 1637 to 1642: a 7.5-turn spiral ramp, no stairs, to a platform at 34.8m. 60 kroner. April to September daily 10:00 to 20:00; October to March to 18:00, to 21:00 Monday and Tuesday with telescope evenings.

places.name: Lilla Ego
places.note: Bib Gourmand 2026 in Vasastan. Order the pork belly at 330 kronor; mains run 315 to 385 and small plates such as scallop or raw beef 185 to 245. Tables are released a month ahead, and it is shut Sunday and Monday.

places.name: Restaurang Pelikan
places.note: Swedish classics on Södermalm, Google 4.3 from 5,661 reviews. Order Pelikans köttbullar, meatballs made by hand in batches of 150kg, at 275 kronor, or the pork knuckle at 295. Open every day 11:30 to 01:00, weekday lunch 11:30 to 13:30.

places.name: Kajsas Fisk
places.note: A fish-soup counter inside the Hötorgshallen market hall, Google 4.6 from 3,924 reviews; the soup is 120 kronor. Open 11:00 to 18:00, to 19:00 on Friday and 17:00 on Saturday, and shut on Sunday.

places.name: Östermalms Saluhall
places.note: The Östermalm food hall, with stalls such as Lisa Elmqvist and Beirut Café; Google 4.4 from 6,590 reviews. Free to walk in, but one guide calls the food wildly expensive. Monday to Friday 09:30 to 19:00, Saturday to 17:00, shut Sunday.

places.name: Bar Agrikultur
places.note: Bib Gourmand 2026 bar on Nytorget, open daily from 17:00 until late, the kitchen to 22:00 Sunday to Thursday and 23:00 Friday and Saturday. Some seats are kept for walk-ins. No prices were found, so check the price.

places.name: Vasa Museum
places.note: The 64-gun warship that sank on her maiden voyage in 1628, in a museum opened 15 June 1990. 195 kronor, free under 18. Daily 10:00 to 17:00, Wednesday to 20:00. Online tickets give no queue priority and large bags are refused, so come at opening.

places.name: Royal Palace (Kungliga slottet)
places.note: Built from 1697 by Tessin the Younger and finished by Hårleman: 1,430 rooms, the Treasury with the regalia in the cellar, and the Tre Kronor Museum, opened 1999. About 24 dollars. Hours are given as 10:00 to 16:00 or to 17:00, so confirm.

places.name: Nordic Museum (Nordiska museet)
places.note: Founded by Artur Hazelius in 1873, in a building finished in 1907. 170 kronor, seniors and students 150, and under 18 free on term weekdays; book a time slot online. Daily 10:00 to 17:00, a short walk from the Vasa.

places.name: Swedish History Museum (Historiska)
places.note: Established 1866: the Gold Room, with about 52kg of gold and 200kg of silver including collars from 350 to 500 CE, and the Viking rooms. Shut Mondays, 11:00 to 17:00, Wednesday to 20:00. About 18 dollars, but one page says free, so check the price.

places.name: Hallwyl Museum
places.note: A house museum at about 15 dollars, with short hours: shut Mondays, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 12:00 to 16:00, Wednesday to 19:00, weekends 11:00 to 17:00. Fit it into an afternoon near Östermalms Saluhall.

places.name: Stockholm City Hall (Stadshuset)
places.note: Ragnar Östberg's City Hall of 1911 to 1923: the Nobel banquet is held in the Blue Hall, and the Golden Hall carries over 18 million mosaic tiles. See it on the 45-minute guided tour, about 15 dollars; the tower needs its own ticket booked ahead.

places.name: Stockholm Cathedral (Storkyrkan)
places.note: First mentioned in 1279. Inside are the St George and the Dragon of 1489, made for Sten Sture the Elder, and the 1636 copy of the oldest colour view of Stockholm. Daily 09:30 to 17:00; listed as free, but one visitor paid 120 kronor, so check the price.

places.name: Skansen
places.note: The open-air museum on Djurgården, about 24 dollars. Listed 10:00 to 18:00, with shorter hours outside summer, so confirm the day before. It is under a kilometre from the Vasa and the Nordic Museum, so make it one Djurgården day.

places.name: Nobel Prize Museum
places.note: On Stortorget in Gamla stan, the square of the 1520 Stockholm Bloodbath. About 16 dollars, free on Tuesday from 17:00 to 20:00. Open 10:00 to 19:00, to 21:00 on Friday.

places.name: Moderna Museet
places.note: Modern and contemporary art. Shut Mondays; 10:00 to 18:00, to 20:00 on Tuesday and Friday, with free entry Friday 18:00 to 20:00. Sources disagree on whether there is a fee at other times, so check the price.

places.name: Monteliusvägen
places.note: A footpath viewpoint, free and open 24 hours, so it costs nothing to fit in. Come late in the day and walk on to dinner at Pelikan or Bar Agrikultur on Södermalm.

places.name: Brasserie Blanche
places.note: A French brasserie. Order the dish of the day at 395 kroner, or the tartare with fries at 385; confit duck is 465. Dinner from 17:00, from 16:00 on Sunday, shut Mondays; the listed 21:00 close looks early, so book and confirm.

places.name: Vaaghals
places.note: Lunch is the way in: two courses for 555 kroner, three for 695, on the menu from 27 October 2026. Lunch Tuesday to Friday to 16:00, dinner Monday to Saturday from 17:00, brunch Saturday 11:00 to 16:00, shut Sunday. Dinner prices were not found.

places.name: Frances Vinbar
places.note: A Bib Gourmand 2026 wine bar. Tuesday to Friday 07:30 to midnight, Saturday from 12:00, Monday 07:30 to 15:00, shut Sunday. No prices were published online, so check the price.

places.name: Akershus Fortress
places.note: Begun in the late 1290s under Haakon V and never taken by siege; it surrendered without a fight in 1940. Grounds open daily 06:00 to 21:00. English tours at weekends, 11:00 and 14:00, about 55 minutes and not on the Oslo Pass; check the price.

places.name: Fram Museum
places.note: Opened 20 May 1936 round the Fram, the ship Colin Archer built to Nansen's specification, and you go aboard her. 180 kroner, children 70. Daily 10:00 to 17:00, every day of the year; tickets on booking.duell.no.

places.name: National Museum (Nasjonalmuseet)
places.note: Opened June 2022, and holds the first version of The Scream, from 1893. About 23 dollars. Shut Mondays; Tuesday and Wednesday 10:00 to 20:00, Thursday to Sunday to 17:00, so use a late evening.

places.name: Munch
places.note: The Bjørvika building opened 22 October 2021, with The Scream, Madonna and The Sick Child among about 28,000 works. Sunday to Tuesday 10:00 to 18:00, Wednesday to Saturday to 21:00. The adult price was not confirmed, so check the price on munch.no.

places.name: Norsk Folkemuseum
places.note: The Norwegian Museum of Cultural History, about 21 dollars, open daily 10:00 to 17:00. It is under a kilometre from the Fram Museum, so do the two in one day.

places.name: Oslo City Hall (Rådhuset)
places.note: Built 1931 to 1950 and opened 15 May 1950; the Nobel Peace Prize is awarded here every 10 December, under main-hall murals by Henrik Sørensen and Alf Rolfsen. Hours and entry were not confirmed, so check the price and times.

places.name: Oslo Cathedral
places.note: Consecrated in November 1697, with ceiling paintings by Hugo Lous Mohr. Open 10:00 to 16:00 except Friday, when it runs 16:00 to midnight. No ticket price is listed; check the price.

places.name: Oslo Ladegård
places.note: A manor from the 1720s on the grounds of the Old Bishop's Palace in Gamlebyen. Hours and entry were not found, so check the price and times before you go.

places.name: Vigeland Sculpture Park, Frogner Park
places.note: Vigeland's 212 bronze and granite sculptures and the 14.12m Monolith of 121 figures, in a park open to the public since 1904. Free and open all year round the clock; Google 4.7 from 23,069 reviews.

places.name: Ekebergparken
places.note: A park with art, free and open 24 hours. One listing says the James Turrell installation opens on Sundays, so go then if you want it.

places.name: Natural History Museum
places.note: About 20 dollars, open daily 10:00 to 17:00. The Botanical Garden is a few minutes away on foot, so do the two together.

places.name: Botanical Garden
places.note: Open daily 07:00 to 17:00, and a review says entry is free. Walk it before the Natural History Museum next door opens at 10:00.

places.name: Holmenkollen Ski Museum
places.note: One ticket, about 20 dollars, covers the ski museum and the Jump Tower. Daily 10:00 to 16:00, so go up in the morning and keep the afternoon for the city.

places.name: Mathallen Oslo
places.note: Oslo's food hall: fish soup with bread at Fiskeriet is 120 to 150 kroner, a smørbrød 75 to 130, a hot bowl 140 to 170. A full meal is 150 to 250 kroner (one source); 200 is the midpoint. Tuesday to Saturday 10:00 to 20:00, Sunday from 11:00, shut Monday. Some stalls close earlier.

places.name: Christiansborg Palace ruins and tower
places.note: Bishop Absalon built the first castle here in 1167; its ruins lie under the palace of 1907 to 1928 and have been open since 1924. Ruins 80 kroner, under 18 free; the tower is free. Ruins Tuesday to Sunday 10:00 to 17:00 in winter, shut Monday. Tower queues are shortest at opening.

places.name: Frederik's Church (Marble Church)
places.note: Frederik V laid the first stone in 1749; it stood unfinished for a century until Tietgen paid and Meldahl finished it in limestone, opening 1894. Free to enter; the dome climb is 35 kroner at 13:00 on weekends. Monday to Thursday and Saturday 10:00 to 17:00, Friday from 12:00, Sunday from 13:00.

outings.why: The year-round B1 from Aker Brygge loops Hovedøya, Lindøya, Gressholmen, Bleikøya and Nakkholmen in about 54 minutes, roughly every 30 minutes; Hovedøya is 8 minutes out. A Zone 1 single, 42 kroner in 2023, or the 24-hour pass.
outings.name: Oslofjord islands on Ruter ferry B1
outings.season: Year-round; the B2 to Langøyene runs May to early September

destination.name: Scandinavia: Copenhagen, Stockholm and Oslo
destination.pitch: Three capitals a train ride apart, made for a history trip: Christian IV's Copenhagen, the Vasa and the Royal Palace in Stockholm, Akershus and the Fram in Oslo. Two or three nights each, and budget hard.
destination.caveat: All three are expensive: Oslo mains run 345 to 495 kroner and Copenhagen hotels average about 230 dollars a night. The Viking Ship Museum is shut until 2027. Copenhagen to Stockholm is about 5 hours by train and to Oslo about 8. Prices use January 2026 rates. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Nyhavn and Rundetaarn's ramp in Copenhagen, Stortorget and the Monteliusvägen view in Stockholm, the Munch in Bjørvika and Vigeland's Frogner Park in Oslo.
because.food: Smørrebrød at Domhusets and Pluto's sharing menu in Copenhagen, Pelikan's meatballs and the fish soup at Kajsas Fisk in Stockholm, lunch at Vaaghals in Oslo.
because.culture: Rosenborg's Crown Jewels and the National Museum's Sun Chariot in Copenhagen; the Vasa, the Gold Room and Storkyrkan's 1489 St George in Stockholm; Akershus, the Fram and the 1893 Scream in Oslo.
